lesson.menu_title: The British Client in Real Time
lesson.menu_desc: Buying time, holding the floor and asking for clarification without freezing -- 33 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 13 -- The British Client in Real Time
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Gustavo Marinho de Carvalho | Lesson 13 -- The British Client in Real Time

listenings.text: Most professionals who freeze in a second language are not missing words. They are missing time. A native speaker who needs three seconds to think fills those seconds with something: that's a good question, let me think about that, off the top of my head. A learner usually fills them with silence, and the silence feels much longer to the speaker than it does to the listener. So the first thing I teach is not grammar. It is five or six phrases that buy time. You say one of them, slowly, and while you are saying it, your brain is already working on the answer. The second thing is permission to rephrase. Nobody speaks in perfect sentences in real time, not even in their first language. If a sentence goes wrong, stop and say, let me rephrase that. It sounds confident, not weak. People who think on their feet are not faster thinkers. They just never leave the floor empty.

I have managed projects with partners from about fifteen countries, and here is something people from outside the UK often get wrong about us. In a British meeting, a pause is not a problem. If you stop for three or four seconds to think, nobody will jump in, and nobody will think less of you. What makes us uncomfortable is something different. It is when somebody answers a question they have not understood, quickly and with confidence, and two weeks later we discover that they were answering a different question. So my advice to any supplier is simple. If you are not sure what the client means, ask. Just to make sure I've understood, are you asking about the cost or the timing? That one sentence has saved more projects than any software I have ever bought. And when you have finished your point, say so. I hope that answers your question is perfectly fine. It tells us it is our turn to speak.
